local_patches.why: GB10 exposes no NVML memory clock; fall back to 273 GB/s for humming's tuning heuristic
VLLM_HUMMING_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 turns on humming's deterministic MoE kernels without the global batch-invariant mode (which forces CUTLASS W4A4 on W4A16 linears)
batch-invariant MoE tuning entries with fewer than 8 warps per CTA run 2 CTAs per SM when their shared memory fits twice; only the persistent grid grows, tile K order is unchanged

local_patches.file: vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/ssd_pinned_configs.py (+ pins in ssd_state_passing.py, ssd_bmm.py, ssd_chunk_scan.py, ssd_chunk_state.py)
local_patches.why: Triton autotune picked different SSD tile configs per boot on GB10, making the same prompt yield one of two token streams; each kernel is pinned to one config (VLLM_MAMBA_SSD_AUTOTUNE=1 restores autotuning)

routed NVFP4 experts are no longer zero-padded (N to 256, K to 128; 9.4% of expert bytes) and use explicit batch-invariant humming tuning configs tuned on GB10, and relu^2 runs as one fused kernel; outputs stay bit-identical (VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_FAST=0 restores the stock padding and heuristic)
skip the MTP drafter when every request in the batch has max_tokens == 1: its drafts are never verified, and the drafter's pass over the prompt delayed the sampled token (the timed prefill)

async spec decode: the verify's and the first single-token draft step's CPU seq_lens are computed from host values the GPU correction kernels were given instead of read back from the GPU (each readback waited for all queued work and left the GPU idle while the CPU planned); the drafter's builders wait on an event before reusing pinned staging. Same integers into every FlashInfer plan (VLLM_HOSTFAST_S1=0 / VLLM_HOSTFAST_S2=0 disable; VLLM_HOSTFAST_CHECK=1 reads back and compares)

engine core: automatic GC paused while it has work (young generations collected while the CPU waits for the GPU), and its threads pinned to the highest-capacity cores after startup (VLLM_HOSTFAST_GC=0 / VLLM_HOSTFAST_PIN=0 disable)

spec-decode verifies stored the fp32 SSM state of every draft position ((d+1) x 2 MiB per Mamba layer) although the next verify reads one; slot 0 now keeps the state after token 0, slot 1 a ring of the 16-bit token inputs, and the next verify replays the accepted tokens with the reference's update and launch config, bit-identical (VLLM_MAMBA_SPEC_REPLAY=0 restores the reference kernel)

Restore submission 766c5c7e FULL uniform speculative-verify graph support and single-request exact graph capture sizes on the tuned MoE/host/Mamba-replay bundle b9a63f4f. Planner, attention arithmetic and model formats remain unchanged.

the Mamba-2 selective_state_update kernel launched with the generic (BLOCK_SIZE_M 4, 4 warps) fallback on GB10; one warp per 4-row tile is what the H100 and B200 float32 files hold for this shape and is about 2x faster on GB10 for a 1- and a 4-token update; the earlier GB10 checks of submission 486ff89d found outputs and states bit-equal to the 4-warp launch (the sm_121 fallback keeps the choice if the device-name lookup finds no file)

one request over the model's 6144 conv channels launched 24 CTAs of 256 channels on a 48-SM GB10; on sm_121 with one request the update kernel now uses 128-channel tiles (48 CTAs). Every channel is computed independently, so no value changes (other devices and batches keep 256).

the tuned routed experts padded K to a multiple of 128, so the down projection's K 1856 became 1920 and every w2 tile streamed and multiplied two all-zero 32-wide K blocks; K now pads only to humming's BF16 pack granule (32), the smallest it accepts. Each element keeps the same K blocks in the same order; the dropped steps were mma(+0, +0, acc), which only turned an acc of -0 into +0, and a signed zero changes no later value's magnitude, logit or token
rkit rebased pack: 10-nlp.diff, 20-relu2.diff, 40-guards.diff. Drafter relu2 can change last bits; target arithmetic and frozen formats unchanged. In-process base consumes hostov when reported.

Pin the MTP predictor to ONE Inductor combo-kernel choice in its own compilation context: combined kernels, never benchmarked (combo_kernels=True, benchmark_combo_kernel=False; VLLM_MTP_COMBO=off pins separate kernels, =bench restores the timed pick). Drafter reduction order is fixed across boots, with target compilation settings and frozen formats unchanged.

Drafter-only greedy head over the shared NVFP4 lm_head: partial-K screen on 64 of 168 fp4 groups (chosen at load from weights only), top-32 per 2048-row chunk, full-K fp32 rescore with bf16 rounding and lowest-id ties. Load-time copies of the checkpoint's own lm_head bytes and scales; the target's lm_head, logits and verification are untouched. VLLM_MTP_SCREEN=0 restores the stock draft head.

Capture an input-independent whole-forward CUDA graph at boot for fresh single-request 496-token prefill, with native FlashInfer planning and fully refreshed request buffers; other lengths and target formats remain unchanged.

Own GB10 prefill two-stage SSD: fuse chunk-state formation with unchanged FP32 state recurrence, and compute each CB row tile once per group in registers before all eight head scans. Removes raw chunk-state and FP32 CB global scratch while retaining every boundary state, cumsum, final gather, original numerical formats and target acceptance. Chunk sizes 128/256 and exact-shape guards; unsupported layouts retain the original path.

Cascade the accepted 4e916237-ea0f-48f5-8cd6-503252f54bc8 draft screen: 32 importance-ranked groups score the complete vocabulary, keep 256 per 2048-row chunk, recompute original 64-group scores for those candidates, then retain 32 per original chunk for the unchanged full-K rescore/BF16/min-ID chain. The wider intermediate set is informed by the negative smaller-screen evidence of b27645a4-0e5b-477b-9502-933cb2eb8a79, without an assumed recall guarantee. New buffers contain exact input-independent NVFP4 byte/scale subsets. No target/native-MTP weights, formats or verification changes. Additional proposal pruning and gathered partial-score lowering can change drafts; recall, exact-token result and speed require official remote validation. VLLM_MTP_SCREEN_CASCADE=0 retains the original single screen.

on GB10 the fp32 MoE router GEMM of the 4-row verify (M 4, N 128, K 2688) ran as cuBLAS gemmSN_TN on 16 CTAs (24 us per layer, 69 GB/s); the vllm::smallk_router_gemm op runs the same summation tree (fma chains over k = 256 j + r + 16 i, tiles then the 16 lanes added in ascending order, recovered by cancellation probes) on 128 CTAs (about 9 us). Bit-identical on the 23 real gate weights (0 of 2.8M outputs differ); any other shape runs torch.mm(x, weight.t()), the call inductor made before (SMALLK=0 or SMALLK_ROUTER=0 disables)

the MoE gate GEMM ran before the shared experts' side stream forked, alone on the GPU; the fp32 gate input (the same cast, still in the compiled graph) now enters the MoE custom op and the runner applies the gate after the fork, so the shared-expert GEMMs overlap it. Same kernels on the same inputs; only the stream schedule changes (SMALLK_EARLY_ROUTER=0 restores it)

smallk's fused sigmoid top-k + moe_align kernel (bit-identical to ops.grouped_topk and the two align kernels for <= 32 ids) is off by default: the routing chain overlaps the shared-expert GEMMs, so shortening it gave no end-to-end gain (SMALLK_TOPK=1 SMALLK_ALIGN=1 enable it)

Compose the promoted boot-captured cascade with the exact native E2M1 pair decoder (including reference zero behavior), BF16/min-ID/NaN selector and two-stage rows-dot launch setting from published ae98b095-4cfd-4d97-bfbf-4a3209f1e6ec. Preserve the promoted 32-group coarse screen, 256 coarse survivors, 64-group refinement and 32 final survivors per chunk. No new pruning, target math or graph lifecycle change.

Fuse tuned indexed expert-up GEMM and ReLU squared in the pinned Humming epilogue. Original BF16 intermediate rounding precedes explicit non-FTZ FP32 ReLU/square and BF16 store. Preserve weight bytes, accumulation, scales and routing; ineligible formats/activations retain original calls. All65536 BF16 patterns and180 realweight cases exact before integration.

Native FP8 small-M Mamba projections with a byte-preserving load-time weight repack. One ascending-K SM120 e4m3 MMA chain per output, scale B then A in FP32, RN BF16. Only fixed two shapes, static scalar scales andM1..8; prefill and other metadata retain CUTLASS. Explicit custom-op boundary preserves runtime shape dispatch under torch.compile. Selected kernel passed1472 cases across23 Mamba layers before integration.

Compose dadon submission 03487090-f839-440b-8b4a-60295374154f (commit 21f55ad0facc8b68dd5934c169f06d069d2f8260): spinning copy-completion event, prefill-only Mamba metadata reuse, single final-state copy, and cuBLAS-order FP32 router for 480/496/512 rows. Byte-exact NVFP4 down-weight packing at load and small-token sparse-sector kernel. Per-call masks skip weight reads only for exact-zero activation sectors, retaining ascending BF16 MMA, FP32 accumulation and original global-scale/RN epilogue. Existing Humming handles unsupported calls and prefill.

zskip: routed-expert w2 for 1..8 tokens without loading the weight k rows whose relu^2 activations are exactly zero in every row routed to the expert. Load-time k-row-major repack of the checkpoint w2 (every byte kept, one k row of a 64-column tile = one 32-byte sector); per call a prep kernel builds each expert block's 16-bit masks and active-group list from that call's activations. Same dequantised bf16 weights (humming's bit placement, x2^124, x scale), one mma.sync.m16n8k16 per k16 group in ascending order from +0 per output (weights as the A operand), skipped rows as +0, empty groups' MMAs omitted, humming's mul.rn.ftz + cvt.rn.bf16x2 epilogue; a -0 accumulator makes the warp recompute densely. Bit-identical to humming on all 23 layers (real decode windows, synthetic, adversarial) and checked against humming at load (4 and 8 tokens); humming keeps prefill. ZSKIP=0 restores routed_sparse.
